price.quote: At a slightly higher price (~$1,999), the Macfox X2 steps up in power and comfort for serious commuters. It’s built on a full-suspension aluminum frame, making it ideal for mixed terrain. Key specs include a 750W motor (1000W peak) and class-3 capability with a top speed of 28 mph.

tq.quote: The Macfox X2 distinguishes itself with its formidable 750W high-power brushless motor, which peaks at an impressive 1000W. Nestled at the bike’s nucleus, this dynamo delivers a remarkable 80nm of torque, ensuring that whether ascending steep slopes or navigating rugged trails, your journey remains fluid, responsive, and invigorating. The motor’s durability is matched only by its ability to conquer the most daunting terrains with sheer ease.
tq.basis: maker blog on the original X2; 80 Nm also in maker blogs 'gear-protection', 'what-is-best-electric-bike-for-california', 'who-makes-best-electric-bicycle-in-usa'. The 65 Nm figure on maker blogs is for the X2 Pro.

sources.quote: Macfox no longer sells the previous X2. The Macfox X2 Pro eBike is the model available today. If you already own an X2 that fits, works properly, and handles your usual routes, there is no reason to replace it just because a Pro version exists.

notes: Given src https://macfoxbike.com/products/macfox-x2 now sells the X2 Pro (different, upgraded model: steel frame, 330 lb limit, $2,199) -- not used for X2 specs. For the original (aluminum, 220 lb) X2 they give 80 Nm (several posts), ~65 lb (gear-protection), and prices ~$1,999 and $1,699; 65 Nm / 330 lb / $2,199-era figures on maker blogs are the X2 Pro.
